categories.main_business_segments: As of the end of 2022, Verisk operates primarily through its Insurance segment, which provides data analytics and decision support solutions to property and casualty (P&C) insurance customers. The company previously operated Energy and Specialized Markets and Financial Services segments, but these were divested in 2022 and early 2023. The Insurance segment now represents approximately 98% of continuing revenues, focusing on underwriting, rating, and claims solutions for the insurance industry.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Verisk leverages advanced technologies including proprietary databases, machine learning, artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and cloud-based software platforms. The company collects, processes, and analyzes billions of records using proprietary data assets and quality control processes, and develops statistical models and actuarial analyses to support insurance underwriting, rating, claims, and catastrophe modeling. Internal software development, remote sensing, and geospatial analytics are also core to its offerings.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Verisk primarily serves the U.S. P&C insurance industry, including all of the top 100 P&C insurers, as well as InsurTech companies, life and annuity insurers, self-insurers, third-party administrators, government agencies, and insurance repair contractors. The company also has a growing presence in international insurance markets, particularly in the UK, Ireland, Canada, and select other regions.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s main operations are in the United States, which accounts for the majority of revenues, with significant operations in the United Kingdom, Canada, Ireland, and expanding presence in Continental Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Asia-Pacific. Verisk maintains offices in over 20 countries and serves customers globally, with a particular focus on North America and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: Verisk operates as a data and analytics service provider, positioned downstream in the insurance value chain. It acts as an information intermediary, aggregating and analyzing data from insurers and other sources to deliver actionable insights, models, and workflow tools directly to insurance carriers, regulators, and related service providers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Verisk’s strategic priorities include expanding solution penetration with existing customers, developing new proprietary data sets and predictive analytics, leveraging intellectual capital to enter adjacent markets, and pursuing targeted acquisitions. The company invests in R&D for new analytic models, digital transformation tools, and international expansion, with a focus on first-to-market innovations and deep integration into customer workflows.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through annual subscriptions and long-term agreements for hosted data and analytics solutions, which are typically prepaid and account for over 81% of revenues. Additional revenue streams include transactional and advisory/consulting services, as well as licensing of proprietary data, software, and actuarial products.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Verisk holds a leading market position in U.S. P&C insurance analytics, with no single competitor matching its breadth of data and services. Key competitors include LexisNexis, CoreLogic, Risk Management Solutions, American Association of Insurance Services, and various regional and specialty technology firms. The company also faces competition from insurers’ internal analytics teams and emerging InsurTech providers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2022, Verisk reported revenues of $2.5 billion, with an EBITDA margin of 65.7% (including gains from divestitures) and a net income margin of 41.7%. The Insurance segment grew revenues by 10.4% year-over-year, with underlying organic growth of 5.8%. The company maintains strong cash flow, significant recurring revenue, and a history of steady growth through both organic initiatives and acquisitions.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Verisk’s value proposition centers on its unique, proprietary data assets, deep domain expertise in insurance, and ability to deliver integrated, first-to-market analytic solutions that are deeply embedded in customer workflows. The company emphasizes the reliability, regulatory compliance, and actionable insights of its solutions, which help insurers improve risk selection, pricing, claims management, and operational efficiency.
